title: The Baal Shem Tov's life
hookLine: a healer and teacher who walked the Carpathian forests

lines: HIS WIFE TAKES IT TO TOWN.
cards: High in the Carpathian mountains, a man is digging clay out of a hillside. Every so often his wife comes with a cart, loads what he has dug, and takes it down to town to sell.
Then he goes back into the trees, alone, for days at a time, to pray and to study. Nobody in the valley thinks of him as anyone special. The stories say that was exactly how he wanted it.

teach.h: ORPHANED, TOLD TO FEAR ONLY GOD.
teach.b: Israel ben Eliezer became known as the Baal Shem Tov. Today, the life the stories tell, mostly from a book of tales collected by people who loved him, In Praise of the Baal Shem Tov.
Historians handle it carefully; it is memory and legend woven together. In the tales, he is orphaned as a small child, and his dying father tells him to fear nothing but God.
As a boy, he keeps slipping away from school into the forest.
As a young man, he works as a teacher's helper, walking the little children to school and back, singing with them along the way.
Later he is a caretaker in a house of study, taken for a simple man, while at night he learns alone.
Then come the hidden years: he and his wife in the mountains, he digging clay and lime, she selling it, and he spending long days in the forests in prayer and solitude.

Only later, the tales say, does he reveal himself as a teacher. A baal shem, a master of the Name, was a familiar figure in Jewish villages then: a healer who wrote amulets and gave remedies of herbs.

teach.h: A HEALER THE POOR COULD REACH.
teach.b: He was known first as one of these, a healer the poor could reach.
Then students came for the teaching, and he settled in the town of Medzhybizh. The Psalms say, "The heavens declare the glory of God."
The tales suggest that before he taught anyone, the forest taught him: the trees, the streams, the long silence.

how: Hasidim retell the tales of the Baal Shem Tov's life at meals, gatherings and on the anniversary of his passing, and some make pilgrimages to his grave in Medzhybizh.

practice: If you can, sit near a window or step outside; if not, bring to mind a tree, a sky or water you know well, and simply watch what it does.

A tree stays put and grows, water finds its way around things, the sky holds weather without becoming it: let one of them teach you one thing. If you pray, you can give thanks in your own words for what you see.

wordCard.voice: Baal shem. A village healer who worked with the divine Name, the humble role the Baal Shem Tov held before students came for his teaching. Today's word.
